blockers: Statutory: discretionary programs are created and funded by Congress, and abolishing or converting them requires legislation.

BUILD America 250 Act (H.R. 8870) has cleared committee only; a short-term extension (H.R. 6500) runs to 2026-12-11, and as of 2026-09-15 the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee chairman said the draft reauthorization will not be introduced until after the November 2026 election, per Bloomberg Government.
Inference: authorizers of both parties and local governments have historically favored keeping some discretionary programs, which makes a wholesale shift to formulas unlikely.

proposal: The Mandate recommends abolishing DOT's discretionary grant-making processes in favor of formula distributions to the states, or at a minimum consolidating the number of grants, and shifting more transportation financing to user fees and private capital. It also asks the Build America Bureau to keep strict underwriting if its loan program continues.
remaining: Congress would need to enact a reauthorization or other statute that ends or consolidates discretionary programs and shifts funds to state formulas; the House committee bill keeps many discretionary programs, the House FY2027 appropriations bill continues BUILD funding, and neither has had a floor vote.
Enactment of a long-term reauthorization or another extension before the extension expires on 2026-12-11.

The administration's own request pairs consolidation of some programs and one formula conversion (SS4A) with three new discretionary programs, so a wholesale shift to formulas is not what it has proposed.
Any change to Build America Bureau lending standards that the Mandate describes is a separate step (the 2026-07-22 letter addresses the TIFIA and RRIF credit programs but not Bureau underwriting).

status_summary: No law or DOT action abolishing discretionary grants or converting them to state formulas has been found. Secretary Duffy's letter of 2026-07-22 asks Congress to consolidate many competitive programs (including merging the Rural, INFRA, Mega and BUILD programs into two multimodal programs) and to convert Safe Streets and Roads for All to a formula program, while also proposing three new discretionary programs. The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee ordered the BUILD America 250 Act (H.R. 8870) reported 62-2 on 2026-05-22 with a larger bridge formula program and a transit block grant but several discretionary programs retained and a new discretionary grant added, and the bill has had no floor action; the House Appropriations Committee's FY2027 bill (H.R. 9170, reported 2026-06-05) provides $550 million for BUILD grants. Surface transportation programs are extended through 2026-12-11 under Public Law 119-103 (signed 2026-09-02), and DOT announced $426 million in INFRA grants on 2026-10-01.

timeline.event: The reconciliation law (Public Law 119-21) is signed; a law-firm summary says it rescinds funding for several transportation grant programs created or funded under prior laws, including most of the Neighborhood Access and Equity Grant Program. This reduces some discretionary funding but does not convert any program to state formulas.

Senate Environment and Public Works Chairman Capito outlines principles for the surface transportation reauthorization: reduce overlapping federal programs, steer more money to highway formula programs states can plan around, and avoid top-down mandates; she also notes a backlog of more than 3,200 awarded discretionary grants without signed agreements.

DOT releases its FY2027 budget request documents. The Budget Highlights keep the core Federal-aid Highway Program at $64.7 billion, distributed mainly by formula, request $770 million for INFRA (competitive) and $713.7 million for the Bridge Formula Program, set National Infrastructure Investments (the BUILD line), Rural and Tribal Infrastructure Advancement and the Federal-State Partnership rail line at zero, request $1.2 billion for Capital Investment Grants (down from $1.7 billion in FY2026), and do not propose consolidating surface grant programs or include a reauthorization proposal (release date from DOT's budget page; the Highlights page was last updated 2026-05-05).

A Congressional Research Service report on the FY2027 DOT budget request describes the request as ending the discretionary programs funded by IIJA multiyear advance appropriations and cutting annual appropriations for some others (BUILD and MEGA from $145 million in FY2026 to zero; Capital Investment Grants from $1.7 billion to $1.2 billion). It does not describe any program being converted to formula funding, and it shows the Bridge Formula Program at $714 million, down from $5.5 billion per year under the IIJA.

H.R. 8870, the BUILD America 250 Act, is introduced by Rep. Graves with Reps. Larsen, Rouzer, Webster and Norton as cosponsors and referred to the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. The introduced text rewrites the bridge program as a formula program (authorized at $9.2 billion a year for FY2027 to FY2031, with a separate $2 billion a year competitive bridge program), creates a transit consolidated state block grant (Sec. 3006), authorizes a Surface Transportation Accelerator Grant (Sec. 1124) and authorizes Safe Streets and Roads for All at $500 million rising to $1 billion (Sec. 1119) (as read from the introduced version; the committee approved an amended bill).

House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee approves the BUILD America 250 Act (H.R. 8870) after a 14-hour markup; the committee's release gives no vote tally and says the chairman plans to bring the bill to the floor soon. The committee's section-by-section summary describes a bridge formula program with set-asides, a transit consolidated state block grant, a pilot letting up to ten states receive their base highway apportionment as a lump sum, a new discretionary Surface Transportation Accelerator Grant, a codified Safe Streets and Roads for All program that remains a grant program, and repeal of several grant programs (for example Neighborhood Access and Equity). A law-firm summary reports a 62-2 vote (other reports give 61-2), about $580 billion over FY2027 to FY2031 ($474.4 billion from the Highway Trust Fund), and some program consolidation (for example three intercity rail programs into one).

The House Appropriations Committee reports H.R. 9170, the FY2027 THUD appropriations bill (H. Rept. 119-686; full committee markup on 2026-06-03 per CRS). The reported text provides $550 million for the National Infrastructure Investments (BUILD) discretionary grant program, derived from unobligated infrastructure-law culvert program balances, against $145 million enacted for FY2026 and no request (CRS); the bill has had no House floor action.

Secretary Duffy sends the chairs and ranking members of three Senate committees the administration's surface transportation reauthorization priorities. The letter proposes consolidating many competitive grant programs, converting Safe Streets and Roads for All to a formula program, eliminating the Mass Transit Account, adding three new discretionary programs, and raising the RRIF cap and replenishing private activity bond authority; it does not name the Build America Bureau. Read in full from the copy hosted by ARTBA, a road builders' trade association; the letter proposes no state block grants and names SS4A as its only explicit conversion to formula, and also proposes dropping the Carbon Reduction competitive program in favor of the CMAQ formula program.

timeline.event: The President signs H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027, which funds agencies through 2026-12-11 and extends authorities including surface transportation, per the White House statement. The enrolled text on GovInfo shows Division C is the Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2026 (Secs. 3001 to 3201), with appropriations and most extensions running to 2026-12-11 and Highway Trust Fund expenditure authority to 2026-12-12; a Congressional Research Service report of 2026-09-14 identifies the current extension of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act authorizations through 2026-12-11 as P.L. 119-103. Associated Press via Transport Topics reports that the House passed it 370-48 on 2026-09-01 after Senate approval. A long-term reauthorization has not been enacted.

Bloomberg Government reports that Senate Environment and Public Works Chairman Capito said the committee's draft surface transportation reauthorization will not be released until after the November 2026 election, citing other priorities such as permitting reform; the article does not discuss formula funds.
DOT announces $426 million in INFRA grants for freight and highway projects in 12 states, showing that DOT continues to award grants under a program it administers by application.

title: Replace DOT discretionary grants with formula distributions to the states
uncertainties: The 2026-07-22 letter was read from the PDF as posted by ARTBA (a road builders' trade association), not by DOT, so section-level details such as the SS4A conversion and the program merger lists rest on that copy (an official DOT copy was searched for and not found); a law firm summary (Holland & Knight, 2026-07-27) does not name the programs to be consolidated and does not mention the SS4A conversion, which the letter itself contains. The introduced text of H.R. 8870 and the committee's section-by-section and release were read, but the committee-reported text was not; GovInfo BILLSTATUS (read 2026-10-22) shows the committee ordered the bill reported as amended by a 62-2 vote on 2026-05-22, lists no committee report number, and shows no House floor or Senate action. The public law text on GovInfo confirms that H.R. 6500 became Public Law 119-103, approved 2026-09-02, with Division C extending surface transportation programs through 2026-12-11. DOT's FY2027 request (2026-04-03) keeps the core highway program on formulas, funds INFRA and sets the BUILD line to zero, and CRS shows the Bridge Formula Program cut sharply as well as discretionary programs, so the request does not read as a shift to formulas. The Senate side is described only through Chairman Capito's 2025-07-16 principles (which favor highway formula programs and cutting overlapping programs) and a Bloomberg Government report of 2026-09-15 quoting the chairman that the draft will not be introduced until after the election; no Senate authorization or THUD bill text was found as of 2026-10-22. H.R. 9170 was read through BILLSTATUS, CRS and part of the reported text; BILLSTATUS gives no committee vote date, and the 2026-06-03 markup date is from CRS. Not checked: DOT grant-condition changes in 2025, FY2026 appropriations structure, and Build America Bureau lending practices. The stage rests on a legislative request, not an enacted change, and is a judgment since the Mandate's primary recommendation (abolish, use formulas) is broader than the request.
